circles.differentiator_line: Practice the way. Explore honestly. Carry it into life.
circles.capacity_note: Each Circle includes only six to eight people. Everyone has a short conversation before placement so we can answer questions and form groups thoughtfully.
circles.quote: Not just a conversation about spiritual life. A shared practice of living it.
circles.description:
Traditional small groups can offer meaningful friendship and learning. Homeward Circles build on that foundation by adding something often missing: a shared practice of spiritual transformation.

Over eight weeks, the same six to eight people learn time-tested forms of Christian meditation and contemplation that can gradually reshape attention and response—helping us become less reactive, more present, and more receptive to God.

A facilitator guides the conversation, but no one person holds all the answers. We speak from lived experience, listen deeply, and learn from the wisdom that emerges through the group—not by debating toward agreement.

Each week, we carry one simple practice into daily life and return to reflect together. Over time, we begin to notice God, connection, meaning, awe, and wonder in ordinary moments—and increasingly see and respond through the mind of Christ.

founder.heading: A fellow traveler.
paragraphs: I studied religion in college and have spent about thirty years in retreats, meditation, and contemplative practice. Along the way I also ran and grew a successful multi-site manufacturing business — but the thing I longed for most, I kept not finding.

In church after church I found beautiful worship and often a genuinely good message. What was missing was the deeper part: the transformative practices that have formed people for centuries, and honest space to bring doubt, ask hard questions, and wrestle with faith out loud. That wrestling is how faith becomes your own — how we come to know God, and ourselves, more deeply.
Homeward is the community I was looking for. I'd love to find the people who've been looking for it too.
founder.disclaimer: Homeward isn't meant to be about one person. I'm simply leading at the start so trust can form and other voices can emerge.

rooted_line: Rooted in the life and way of Jesus, Homeward welcomes people with faith, questions, doubt, and uncertainty who are sincerely open to spiritual growth.

items: Remembering to slow down and return to the present.
Remembering that God is near—even in ordinary moments.
Remembering to choose love, compassion, and courage.
Remembering that we do not have to make the journey alone.
remembering.heading: We gather
remembering.why_text: A community helps our practices stay alive. As we return together, our attention changes and we become more open to God, love, connection, peace, awe, and wonder in the life already in front of us.
remembering.intro1: Homeward began because many people had heard meaningful ideas about God and love but still longed for a way to experience them more deeply in everyday life.
remembering.intro2: We come together to help one another remember what matters most—and keep returning to the practices that make that remembering real.
remembering.footer_text: Maybe you have been looking for people who will help you keep returning, too.

faq.heading: Questions are welcome. Here are a few clear answers.

items.question: What do you mean by “rooted in Jesus”?
items.answer: We return continually to the life, teachings, and way of Jesus as the center of our shared practice. People do not have to arrive with identical beliefs or settled certainty, but they should be sincerely open to exploring Jesus and participating respectfully in a Jesus-centered community.

items.question: What if the word “God” is difficult for me?
items.answer: You are welcome to begin honestly. Some people come with a clear Christian faith. Others are questioning, rebuilding, or more comfortable speaking about a Higher Power or an openness to something beyond themselves. Homeward remains rooted in Jesus, but no one is required to pretend certainty or use identical language.

items.question: What are Christian meditation and contemplative prayer?
items.answer: They are time-tested ways of becoming quiet, attentive, and open to God. Practices may use the breath, a prayer word, Scripture, reflection, visualization, gratitude, or silent presence. No prior experience is needed; we learn by practicing together.

items.question: Do you draw from traditions outside Christianity?
items.answer: Homeward is rooted in Jesus and draws primarily from the historic Christian contemplative tradition. We also acknowledge that practices such as silence, attention, compassion, gratitude, and awareness of the breath appear in other traditions. We engage those points of connection honestly and respectfully without turning Homeward into a blend of religions.

items.question: Is Homeward a church?
items.answer: Homeward is forming as a Jesus-centered spiritual community, beginning with Circles. You do not need to leave an existing church, and you do not need previous church involvement to participate.

items.question: Why is a conversation required before joining a Circle?
items.answer: The conversation gives you a chance to ask questions and understand the experience before committing. It also helps us learn what you are seeking, confirm that the Circle posture is a good fit, and thoughtfully match people into groups. We are looking for openness and a desire to grow—not doctrinal certainty.

recognition.heading: Does any of this feel familiar?
recognition.intro: Many of us have heard meaningful teachings about God, a Higher Power, love, and transformation. What we were missing was a way to practice them—and people to walk with us.
questions: You still feel drawn to God—or to the life and way of Jesus—but carry questions or doubts you have never been able to resolve?
You long to experience God—or a Higher Power—more deeply, not simply gather more religious information?
You want spiritual practices that help you become more present, peaceful, loving, and awake in everyday life?
You are looking for a community where people learn from one another without being required to reach all the same conclusions?
recognition.honest_line: You do not need settled beliefs—only an honest desire to explore, practice, and grow.

items.title: Light of Christ
items.description: A guided meditation in which we receive the loving light of Christ, rest in that presence, and allow the light to radiate toward those we love, the wider world, and all creation.

items.title: Breath Prayer
items.description: A simple prayer joined to the natural rhythm of breathing—such as, “Breathing in, I receive peace. Breathing out, I offer love.”

items.title: Maranatha Prayer
items.description: Silently repeating Maranatha—Come, Lord Jesus as a way of gathering the mind, releasing distraction, and welcoming the presence of God.

items.title: Inspired Reading
items.description: A time-honored method and practice for reading Scripture and listening for the words, images, or invitations that speak to your life.

items.title: Daily Reflection
items.subtitle: Noticing God in your day
items.description: A five-step process for reviewing your day with gratitude and honesty, noticing where you felt alive, distant, loved, or invited to grow.

items.title: Prayer of Gratitude
items.description: A gentle practice of remembering the gifts, people, and moments that have sustained us—and allowing gratitude to widen our awareness of God’s goodness.

practices.heading: The missing how-to of spiritual life.
practices.intro: Homeward practices are simple, guided ways of training attention, opening to God, and bringing the way of Jesus into ordinary life. No prior experience is needed; we learn by practicing together.
practices.more_text: And more—including Inspired Reading, Daily Reflection, and Prayer of Gratitude.

hero.headline: Journeying Toward God.
hero.description:
Homeward is a Jesus-centered community where time-tested practices help us open our hearts, quiet our minds, and deepen our connection with God—bringing more love, joy, and aliveness into everyday life.

In guided Circles, we practice Christian meditation and contemplation, reflect on scripture through honest conversation, and learn to carry the way of Jesus into how we live and love.
